description: Predicate 4a SAT — market-share defensibility. Three pricing moves (raise_price, freemium, no_change) projected against two competitors who each have 3 response postures (aggressive cut / match / no change). With floor_threshold=0.25, only 'freemium' (projected share 0.50) absorbs the worst-case combined competitor impact (0.08 + 0.05 = 0.13) and still stays above the floor. 'raise_price' (0.32) and 'no_change' (0.30) both get knocked under 0.25 under aggressive double-cut. Unique durable winner: freemium.
_solver_note: Manual skolemization over the Cartesian product of competitor responses (3 x 3 = 9 combos). Share floor inequality: my_share - sum(competitor_response_impact) >= floor_threshold. Only freemium survives the worst-case 0.08+0.05=0.13 combined impact (0.50 - 0.13 = 0.37 >= 0.25). raise_price collapses (0.32 - 0.13 = 0.19 < 0.25), no_change collapses (0.30 - 0.13 = 0.17 < 0.25).
